title: Scale Onramp: Seller Playmap (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, scannable playmap sellers can carry from initial qualification through pilot and into reserved capacity deals. This is a lightweight, workshopable sketch — not the final enablement deck.

Audience:
- Platform engineers and infra architects (primary)
- Product managers and AI feature owners (secondary)
- Sales engineer + AE enablement

Goal:
- Convert 1st pilot to paid reserved capacity with clear success metrics and low friction ops handoff.

One-line pitch sellers can use:
'Redwood gives you predictable latency and cost controls for LLMs so your product ship cadence and SLOs don't get blocked by inference variability.'

Customer scenarios & scripts (short):
1) High-throughput embeddings pipeline (search):
  - Qualify: "What initial QPS and peak-hour batch sizes do you expect?"
  - Tech signal: embeddings per second, batch sizes, typical sequence length.
  - Value props to call out: autoscaling + batching profiles, cost-per-embedding guidance, KV cache to avoid re-embedding repeated inputs.
  - Objection tactic: If they say "we can self-host cheaper" -> ask about engineering ops cost, SLA risk, and fallback policy for regen.

2) Customer-facing chat assistant (low-latency):
  - Qualify: "target tail latency for 95/99th percentile?"
  - Tech signal: single-request latency SLO, token lengths, expected concurrency.
  - Value props: dedicated pools, regional routing, canary rollouts, streaming support.
  - Objection tactic: If "latency too high" -> propose canary on dedicated with reserved baseline + autoscale burst; offer latency bench in-region.

3) Regulated PII workload (security-first):
  - Qualify: "Are you under a regulatory constraint (HIPAA, SOC2) requiring on-prem or VPC?"
  - Tech signal: data residency, KMS/HSM needs, audit log retention.
  - Value props: Private deployment option, customer-managed keys, audit hooks.
  - Objection: "We need air-gapped" -> propose on-prem bundle + professional services kickoff.

Objection handling matrix (quick):
- "Price": show per-token + cost model swap vs self-host (include ops uplift); offer 3-month reserved trial with credits.
- "Latency": routing + dedicated pools + pin model version; run in-region bench.
- "Security/Compliance": map to Private + audit + SOC2; offer checklist.
- "Lock-in": emphasize multi-variant routing and model portability + exportable logs.

Technical qualifiers sellers must capture (fast form):
- QPS / peak TPS, concurrency patterns
- Typical prompt/response token length
- Tail latency SLO (p95/p99), throughput SLOs
- Compliance needs (data residency, retention, KMS)
- Expected start date & success metrics for pilot

Pilot -> Scale checklist (for seller + SE):
[ ] Kickoff: attach sample traffic and prompts (anonymized)
[ ] Baseline bench: perf + cost using our standard model profile
[ ] Success metrics: e.g., p95 < 250ms, cost per 1k tokens <$X, error rate < 0.5%
[ ] Rollout plan: canary %, rollback thresholds, instrumentation hooks
[ ] Procurement blockers: legal + networking + capacity commit timeline

Seller play tips (tone & style):
- Keep it engineering-first: hand the form to the platform engineer; talk SLOs not buzzwords.
- Use concrete numbers early.
- Offer an 'ops-lite' path: start hosted API for 4–6 weeks, then lift-and-shift to Dedicated if needed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add short table of recommended model/quantization combos by workload (TODO: ask Research for recent bench)
- Create one-pager pricing example for embeddings vs chat for three volume tiers (TODO: finance)
- Build two slide visuals: "pilot timeline" and "decision ladder" (action for design)
- Validate legal checklist for Private (Aisha to ping security).

Notes to self:
- Keep this under 2 slides when converted for AE quick deck.
- Follow up with Sofia for bench numbers and with Elliot for sample network checklist.

Suggested next steps (for enablement):
1) Turn this into 2-slide quick pack + 1-page price appendix (owner: Aisha).
2) Run roleplay with SEs and record common pushbacks (owner: Tom).
3) Publish on Confluence and link to SKUs + legal checklist (owner: Sofia).

End of sketch.
